translationRepairs: Early in the Huitong era, as the Taizong Emperor prepared an eastern hunt, Sanke memorialized to cut down the baggage train, hurry to the northern mountains to gather supplies for the treasury, and spare the farmers their labor.

Early in the Huitong era, as the Taizong Emperor prepared an eastern hunt, the Three Commanders memorialized that the baggage train should be reduced and the party should hurry to the northern mountains to gather supplies for the treasury without disrupting farm work.

The proposal correctly removes the invented person Sanke, but the Liao glossary in volume 116 defines 三剋 as a military command office equivalent to 三帥. 'The Three Commanders' is clearer and source-based; the syntax also states the substance of their memorial rather than treating every following verb as their action.

At the beginning of the Huitong era of the Taizong Emperor, when he was about to hunt in the east, Sanke memorialized to reduce baggage trains, hasten to the northern mountains to gather supplies for state use, and not harm agricultural work.

At the beginning of the Huitong era under Emperor Taizong, when he was about to hunt in the east, the Three Commanders memorialized that the baggage train should be reduced and the party should hasten to the northern mountains to obtain supplies for state use without harming agricultural work.
Volume 116 defines 三剋 as an army-commanding office equivalent to 'Three Commanders'; it is neither a personal name nor an unexplained ke rank.

Ma Renwangqian served as expenditure commissioner at Nanjing, where public and private stores alike prospered; he conducted household registration with fair and lenient application of the law, and was then promoted to expenditure commissioner at the Central Capital.

Because Ma Renwang had previously served as judge of the expenditure bureau at Nanjing, where public and private stores alike prospered and he conducted household registration with fair and lenient application of the law, he was then transferred to be expenditure commissioner at the Central Capital.
馬人望前為南京度支判官 marks prior tenure as expenditure-bureau judge; fusing 前 into 'Renwangqian' and calling him 度支使 at Nanjing are errors, and 以…乃遷 is causal transfer correctly restored.

Ma Renwangqian was made expenditure commissioner at Nanjing; public and private affairs were both ample, he inspected and registered households, applied the law with fairness and forbearance, and was then transferred to be expenditure commissioner at the Central Capital.

Because Ma Renwang had previously been judge of the expenditure bureau at Nanjing, public and private affairs were both ample, he inspected and registered households, applied the law with fairness and forbearance, and was then transferred to be expenditure commissioner at the Central Capital.
The proposal rightly splits 馬人望 from 前為 and restores 度支判官 then 度支使, but 'With Ma Renwang…—he was then transferred' is awkward and fails to render causal 以; revise to a clear Because… construction.

When the Tianzuo Emperor was driven into exile, Yelü Dilie and others forced the installation of Prince Liang Yali and ordered the herd-management households to transport grain from the Yanliao granary.

When the Tianzuo Emperor was driven into exile, Yelü Dilie and others forced the installation of Prince Liang Yali and ordered the herd-management households to transport grain from the Salt Marsh granary.
Yanliao is erroneous, but 'Yanbo' is an unsupported reading. Other occurrences in the Liao History render 鹽濼 as Salt Marsh, including the parallel account in volume 30.

When the Tianzuo Emperor was driven into exile, Yelü Dilie and others forced the installation of Prince Liang Yali and ordered the herd-management households to transport grain from the Yanliao granary.

When the Tianzuo Emperor was driven into exile, Yelü Dilie and others forced the installation of Prince Liang Yali and ordered the herd-management households to transport grain from the Salt Marsh granary.
The literal field should follow the established translation of the toponym 鹽濼 as Salt Marsh rather than inventing either Yanliao or Yanbo.

Feng Yanxiu and Han Shaoxun, one after another, pursued commercial profit and sought to impose the same regulations as at Pingshan in the Yan region; the people rebelled, and the great Dazhonglin uprising broke out.

Feng Yanxiu and Han Shaoxun, one after another, pursued commercial profit and sought to impose the same regulations as at Pingshan in the Yan region; the people suffered under them, and Da Yanlin's rebellion followed.
大延琳 is the personal name Da Yanlin, while 其民病之 means the people suffered under the regulations before the rebellion arose.

Feng Yanxiu and Han Shaoxun in succession pursued commercial profit and wished to impose regulations like those at Pingshan in the Yan region; the people suffered under this, and the great rebellion of Dazhonglin arose.

Feng Yanxiu and Han Shaoxun in succession pursued commercial profit and wished to impose regulations like those at Pingshan in the Yan region; the people suffered under this, and the rebellion of Da Yanlin arose.
大延琳 is the personal name Da Yanlin; Dazhonglin misreads 延, and 'great' is not an adjective modifying rebellion here.
